themes_detail.label: Street noise spike in Mott Haven
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 62 THIS WEEK, a 351% spike above the 8-week average of 13.8 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.55), signaling a sudden, concentrated disruption affecting outdoor public spaces.
evidence: 62 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.8 weekly baseline (351% increase)
Z-score of 6.55 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Pattern is acute (this week only), not chronic
reporting_angles: Door-knock reporting: which blocks are affected, what is the source (construction, bars, street vendors, traffic)?
Interview 311 complaint filers and local residents about timing and nature of noise
Check if this coincides with street fairs, construction permits, or new commercial activity filed with DOB

themes_detail.label: Encampment growth in district
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK, a 319% increase from the 8-week average of 2.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.66), reflecting a rapid uptick in visible homelessness across CD 201.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (319% spike)
Z-score of 4.66 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'services for the homeless' (recurring unfunded ask)
reporting_angles: Locate the encampments: where are the 11 complaints clustered? (check 311 map)
Profile residents experiencing homelessness: what pushed numbers up THIS WEEK?
Assess alignment between 311 complaints and actual shelter/service capacity in the district

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK, a 471% jump above the 8-week average of 0.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.88), suggesting either increased street vendor activity or new enforcement action in the district.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (471% increase)
Z-score of 6.88 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Timing suggests either new vendor density or new enforcement action THIS WEEK
reporting_angles: Check with NYC Department of Consumer Affairs: has enforcement changed or expanded THIS WEEK?
Interview street vendors: are they facing new crackdowns or is there a surge in food cart/cart activity?
Map complaint locations to identify which corridors are affected (Grand Concourse, 3rd Ave, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Lead complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead-related complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 700% spike above the 8-week average of 0.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.42), raising concerns about lead exposure in housing stock that may affect children.
evidence: 3 lead complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase)
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'additional building inspectors,' suggesting capacity gap in oversight
reporting_angles: Get specifics on the 3 lead complaints: which properties, what type of lead exposure (paint, water, dust)?
Investigate whether these properties have prior lead violations or DOB inspection history
Interview residents: are families with young children aware of lead risk in their units? Have they been tested?

themes_detail.label: Drug activity complaints rise
themes_detail.summary: Drug Activity complaints jumped to 10 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 248% spike above the 8-week average of 2.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.41), indicating a notable escalation in visible drug-related incidents.
evidence: 10 drug activity complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (248% increase)
Overlaps with encampment spike, suggesting possible correlation
reporting_angles: Cross-check drug activity complaint locations with encampment complaints—are they clustered?
Interview NYPD: has narcotics enforcement changed, or is this reflecting actual increased activity?
Talk to local stakeholders (businesses, block associations, nonprofits) about open-air drug scenes
